task: EPMCDME-13933: index long marketplace assistants as N token-bounded chunks (ES ids <id>_<n>, header repeated per chunk) with write-then-delete stale cleanup, per-entity batch fallback, chunk-wide unpublish delete, and per-assistant de-duplication in marketplace search instead of truncating to fit the embedding context length.

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.affected: AssistantLoader (chunking, header/body split, chunk metadata), BasePlatformLoader (multi-document entity contract), BasePlatformDatasourceProcessor (shared base: chunk ids, grouping, batching with per-entity fallback, stale-chunk delete_by_query, unpublish delete-all-chunks), SearchAndRerankMarketplace (over-fetch, best-chunk-per-assistant dedupe, coverage normalisation, routing limit override)
component_scope.layers: Datasource Loader / Indexing Service, Search Service, DB-Persistence (Elasticsearch)

requirements_clarity.label: M
requirements_clarity.gaps: Design changed mid-flight from truncation to chunking; chunk budget (1500 tokens, 100 overlap), over-fetch factor (3x) and handling of legacy single-document entries were implementation decisions rather than stated acceptance criteria.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: Changed Elasticsearch document identity scheme (<id>_<n>) on a live index with legacy single-doc entries, write-then-delete stale cleanup via delete_by_query (data loss if filter wrong), batch failure fallback semantics, progress counter accounting per chunk on unpublish, search result de-dup with over-fetch affecting ranking/popularity boost and source routing, shared base processor used by other platform datasources
technical_risk.mitigation: Stale delete scoped by metadata.id terms with must_not on just-written ids and conflicts=proceed; delete failures logged not raised; single-entity paths fail fast; extensive unit tests across loader, processor and marketplace search; code review (3 major findings fixed in one round) and live check 13/13 on local stack

key_reasoning.reason: Four components changed across indexing and search: AssistantLoader, the BasePlatformLoader contract, the shared BasePlatformDatasourceProcessor (inherited by all platform datasources), and SearchAndRerankMarketplace. Base M(3), bumped to L(4) because shared base classes were touched.

There was no exact precedent for multi-chunk platform entities. The work changed the ES document id scheme on a live index that still has legacy docs, added destructive delete_by_query stale cleanup and unpublish-all-chunks, and changed search ranking with over-fetch and dedupe. Code review found 3 major findings, which confirms non-trivial risk.
diffstat reports 8 files (4 source + 4 test) across 4 directories, with 791 insertions and 109 deletions. 8 files maps to L under the 7-10 rule.
The design was reworked mid-flight from truncation to chunking, and tuning constants and legacy-doc handling were decided during implementation.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from M to L: touches core shared base classes (BasePlatformLoader contract and BasePlatformDatasourceProcessor used by all platform datasources)
